fields.mechanism: Immediate or delayed physiological intolerance response triggered by vascular occlusion during controlled unilateral fluid suffusion
fields.intervention: Integrate an inline pressure sensor that applies a brief, controlled micro-suffusion test bolus into the infusion line and monitors the downstream pressure-time profile; true downstream occlusion produces an immediate or predictably delayed (up to 25 minutes) monotonic pressure rise matching the intolerance signature reported in the paper, whereas transient patient movement produces non-monotonic, rapidly decaying pressure spikes that do not match this temporal profile.
fields.expected_effect: The pump distinguishes true downstream occlusion from transient patient movement by matching the measured pressure-time curve against the immediate or delayed occlusion-intolerance signature, triggering an alarm and halting flow before patient injury occurs.
fields.falsification_test: Induce complete downstream occlusions and simulated patient-movement artifacts in a benchtop infusion loop; if the micro-suffusion pressure-time profiles for true occlusions fail to exhibit the immediate or 25-minute delayed rise described in the paper, or if patient-movement artifacts produce identical signatures, the mechanism is falsified.

fields.mechanism: Delayed vascular occlusion intolerance occurring after a latency period rather than instantaneously
fields.intervention: Remove the active instantaneous pressure-threshold alarm and replace it with a passive structural compliance chamber downstream of the inline sensor that imposes a fixed 25-minute hydraulic delay, allowing transient patient-movement pressure spikes to dissipate structurally while sustained true occlusion pressure accumulates passively through the chamber until it triggers detection
fields.expected_effect: True downstream occlusions are detected via passive pressure accumulation within the tolerance window before patient harm, while transient movement artifacts decay within the compliance chamber without triggering false alarms
fields.falsification_test: Introduce a complete downstream occlusion and verify that the passive compliance chamber triggers detection within 20 minutes; separately introduce transient pressure spikes simulating patient movement and verify they dissipate within the chamber without triggering detection

fields.mechanism: Immediate or delayed physiological intolerance response to vascular occlusion during controlled fluid delivery
fields.intervention: Program the infusion pump controller to continuously monitor the inline pressure sensor for an immediate sharp rise or a delayed progressive rise over a 25-minute window, mapping these two specific temporal profiles as definitive downstream occlusion signatures rather than using a single static pressure threshold, thereby distinguishing true occlusion from transient patient movement artifacts.
fields.expected_effect: The pump detects both sudden complete blockages and gradual partial blockages before patient harm occurs by recognizing the exact temporal pressure profiles associated with vascular occlusion intolerance, preventing undetected continued infusion against an occluded line.
fields.falsification_test: Induce downstream occlusions in a benchtop flow loop and verify that the pump alarm triggers within the immediate or 25-minute delayed windows matching the reported intolerance profiles; if induced occlusions produce pressure signatures outside these two temporal patterns, the mechanism transfer is falsified.

fields.mechanism: Immediate or delayed vascular occlusion intolerance detected during unilateral fluid suffusion, combined with concurrent hemodynamic and electrical cardiac monitoring to identify flow blockage events.
fields.intervention: Implement a multi-physics hybrid inline sensor combining fluidic pressure measurement with acoustic emission detection at the infusion line; calibrate the dual-domain thresholds using the temporal profile of immediate versus 25-minute delayed occlusion intolerance observed during pulmonary suffusion to differentiate true downstream occlusion (sustained pressure rise plus continuous acoustic cavitation/flow-stop signature) from transient patient movement (brief pressure spike without sustained acoustic change).
fields.expected_effect: The combined fluidic-acoustic detection mechanism distinguishes true downstream occlusion from transient motion artifacts within seconds, triggering pump shutoff before injury occurs and preventing the documented downstream occlusion detection failures.
fields.falsification_test: Induce controlled downstream occlusions and simulated patient movement artifacts on a test bench while recording simultaneous inline pressure and acoustic signals; if the dual-domain algorithm fails to distinguish true occlusion from movement with greater than 99% sensitivity and specificity within 5 seconds, the mechanism is falsified.
